text_nodes.text: Anyone can ride one to the airport now

On October 14th Waymo opened its San Antonio robotaxis to anyone with the app, San Antonio International Airport included. The federal record of its flood recall still lists the remedy as under development. Drawn to illustrate.

text_nodes.text: In February, it came by invitation

Waymo took its first public riders in San Antonio on February 24th, inviting them from the tens of thousands across four cities who had the app. Texas Public Radio put that first service area at 60 square miles. Drawn to illustrate.

text_nodes.text: Texas Public Radio reported an empty Waymo was swept up in flood waters and washed into the creek during heavy rain, and that no one was hurt. Earlier that April another was stranded in floodwater near McCullough Avenue and Contour Drive. Drawn to illustrate.

text_nodes.text: It slowed. Then it drove in

The recall record says the software may let the vehicle slow and then drive into standing water on higher speed roadways. Texas Public Radio reports the notice said it detected the flooded road and kept going. The report reached regulators 11 days after the creek. Drawn to illustrate.

text_nodes.text: Texas Public Radio called the flood pause Waymo's longest in San Antonio to date. On May 10th it reported service was expected to resume that week. On May 13th it reported the cars were running without riders. Drawn to illustrate.

One post for each day from February 24th to October 14th, a row for each month. The blue ring is April 20th. The posts lit after it count the days until the service opened to everyone with the app.

text_nodes.text: Anyone can ride. Anyone can read the remedy field
The city's airports director called the rides a new option to get there. NHTSA's recall record for Waymo LLC is public, and its remedy field still reads under development. Drawn to illustrate.
